style=\"font-family: inherit;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;CASE REPORT-\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\" https:\/\/shaardul124.blogspot.com\/2023\/12\/prefinals-case.html\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;https:\/\/shaardul124.blogspot.com\/2023\/12\/prefinals-case.html\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ELEARNING POINTS-\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1 Difference between rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2 Different etiologies and presentations of vertigo\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E3 Romberg test demonstrating sensory ataxia v cerebellar ataxia-\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit;\"\u003E“\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(33, 33, 33); color: #212121; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EFor sensory ataxia and cerebellar ataxia, their Romberg’s signs are both positive, but there are some differences. The patient can keep standing steady during the eye-opening phase, and standing unsteadily, wobbling, or even falling in the closed eye phase (\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Ca aria-expanded=\"false\" aria-haspopup=\"true\" class=\"bibr popnode\" href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC8046926\/#B12\" rid=\"B12\" role=\"button\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; box-sizing: inherit; color: #4c2c92; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EFranchignoni et al., 1984\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(33, 33, 33); color: #212121; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003E), as shown in\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Ca class=\"fig-table-link figpopup\" co-legend-rid=\"lgnd_F1\" href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC8046926\/figure\/F1\/\" rid-figpopup=\"F1\" rid-ob=\"ob-F1\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; box-sizing: inherit; color: #4c2c92; cursor: pointer; display: inline-block; text-size-adjust: 100%;\" target=\"figure\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"box-sizing: inherit;\"\u003EFigure 1\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(33, 33, 33); color: #212121; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003E. The cerebellar ataxia patients were unstable in the stage of closing eyes and opening eyes, and tend to tilt toward the diseased side of cerebellum”\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(33, 33, 33); color: #212121; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003E“The maintenance of human balance mainly depends on the coordination of vestibular system, visual system and proprioceptive system (\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Ca aria-expanded=\"false\" aria-haspopup=\"true\" class=\"bibr popnode\" href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC8046926\/#B19\" rid=\"B19\" role=\"button\" style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; box-sizing: inherit; color: #4c2c92; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003EMaurer et al., 2001\u003C\/a\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; background-color: white; caret-color: rgb(33, 33, 33); color: #212121; text-size-adjust: 100%;\"\u003E). In an upright position, a normal person can stand steadily when the eyes open and close; but when two or more systems are damaged, the human body will not be able to maintain balance. For example, when a patient is suffering from Sensory Ataxia, the visual system can provide compensation information when the eyes are open, so the patient can remain upright and stable; Visual compensation would disappear when the eyes are closed, patients will not be able to maintain upright stability. This is the theoretical basis of Romberg’s sign“\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC8046926\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC8046926\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E4 Proprioception evaluation\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E5 Vertebrobasillar insufficiency caused by fluorosis\/spondyloarthopathy leading to intermittent vertigo (similar to angina)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit;\"\u003EVERTEBROBASILAR INSUFFICIENCY-\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Ch4 style=\"background-color: white; font-size: 15.9991px; margin: 0.6923em 0px; text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121; font-size: 16px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit;\"\u003E\"\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit; font-weight: normal;\"\u003EVertebrobasilar insufficiency (VBI) is defined by inadequate blood flow through the posterior circulation of the brain, supplied by the 2 vertebral arteries that merge to form the basilar artery. The vertebrobasilar arteries supply the cerebellum, medulla, midbrain, and occipital cortex. When the blood supply to these areas is compromised, it can lead to severe disability and\/or death.\u003Cbr \/\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit; font-weight: normal;\"\u003ESymptoms include:\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cul style=\"background-color: white; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\" style=\"margin: 0.6923em 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit; font-weight: normal;\"\u003EVertigo (the most common symptom)\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul style=\"background-color: white; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\" style=\"margin: 0.6923em 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit; font-weight: normal;\"\u003EDizziness\/syncope: Sixty percent of patients with VBI have at least 1 episode of dizziness.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul style=\"background-color: white; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\" style=\"margin: 0.6923em 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit; font-weight: normal;\"\u003E\"Drop attacks:\" Patient feels suddenly weak in the knees and fall\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul style=\"background-color: white; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\" style=\"margin: 0.6923em 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit; font-weight: normal;\"\u003EDiplopia\/Loss of vision\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul style=\"background-color: white; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\" style=\"margin: 0.6923em 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit; font-weight: normal;\"\u003EParesthesia\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul style=\"background-color: white; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\" style=\"margin: 0.6923em 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit; font-weight: normal;\"\u003EConfusion\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul style=\"background-color: white; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\" style=\"margin: 0.6923em 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit; font-weight: normal;\"\u003EDysphagia\/dysarthria\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul style=\"background-color: white; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\" style=\"margin: 0.6923em 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit; font-weight: normal;\"\u003EHeadache\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul style=\"background-color: white; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\" style=\"margin: 0.6923em 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit; font-weight: normal;\"\u003EAltered consciousness\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul style=\"background-color: white; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\" style=\"margin: 0.6923em 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit; font-weight: normal;\"\u003EAtaxia\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul style=\"background-color: white; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\" style=\"margin: 0.6923em 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit; font-weight: normal;\"\u003Econtralateral motor weakness\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul style=\"background-color: white; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\" style=\"margin: 0.6923em 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit; font-weight: normal;\"\u003ELoss of temperature and pain\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003Cul style=\"background-color: white; font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E\u003Cli class=\"half_rhythm\" style=\"margin: 0.6923em 0px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit; font-weight: normal;\"\u003EIncontinence\"\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/li\u003E\u003C\/ul\u003E\u003C\/h4\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-size: 15.9991px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK482259\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/books\/NBK482259\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit;\"\u003EFLUOROSIS-\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit;\"\u003EOur patient is from a fluorosis endemic area.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121; font-size: 16px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit;\"\u003E\"Endemic skeletal fluorosis is a chronic metabolic bone and joint disease caused by ingesting large amounts of fluoride either through water or rarely from foods of endemic areas. Fluoride is a cumulative toxin which can alter accretion and resorption of bone tissue. It also affects the homeostasis of bone mineral metabolism. The total quantity of ingested fluoride is the single most important factor which determines the clinical course of the disease which is characterized by immobilization of joints of the axial skeleton and of the major joints of the extremities. A combination of osteosclerosis, osteomalacia and osteoporosis of varying degrees as well as exostosis formation characterizes the bone lesions.\"\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #212121; font-family: inherit;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/3295994\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/3295994\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit;\"\u003ECERVICAL SPONDYLOSIS-\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121; font-size: 16px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit;\"\u003E\"Cervical spondylosis is a term that encompasses a wide range of progressive degenerative changes that affect all the components of the cervical spine (i.e., intervertebral discs, facet joints, joints of Luschka, ligamenta flava, and laminae). It is a natural process of aging and presents in the majority of people after the fifth decade of life. Symptoms of cervical spondylosis manifest as neck pain and neck stiffness and can be accompanied by radicular symptoms when there is compression of neural structures\"\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #212121; font-family: inherit;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/31855384\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/31855384\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #212121; font-family: inherit;\"\u003EOSSIFICATION OF POSTERIOR LONGITUDINAL LIGAMENT-\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit;\"\u003E\"Patients with myelopathy often give a history of changes in balance and fine motor skills (worsening handwriting, difficulty buttoning buttons). As myelopathy progresses, patients may require ambulatory aids or a wheelchair. During the physical examination, the clinician should assess both the Rhomberg and tandem gait tests to identify early signs of gait or balance dysfunction. Brisk reflexes as well as clonus may be present in the upper and lower extremities\"\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #212121;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC4771496\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC4771496\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #212121;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003EOSSIFICATION OF POSTERIOR LONGITUDINAL LIGAMENT AND ASSOCIATION WITH FLUOROSIS-\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121; font-size: 16px;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit;\"\u003E\"Fluorosis is associated with a higher incidence of OPLL.\"\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #212121; font-family: inherit;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/30233012\/#:~:text=The%20continuous%20variant%20of%20OPLL,a%20higher%20incidence%20of%20OPLL.\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/30233012\/#:~:text=The%20continuous%20variant%20of%20OPLL,a%20higher%20incidence%20of%20OPLL.\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #212121; font-family: inherit;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003ECASE REPORTS OF FLUOROSIS CAUSING CERVICAL MYELOPATHY-\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #212121; font-family: inherit;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white;\"\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.jocn-journal.com\/article\/S0967-5868(08)00501-8\/fulltext\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.jocn-journal.com\/article\/S0967-5868(08)00501-8\/fulltext\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #212121; font-family: inherit;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/nimhans.ac.in\/wp-content\/uploads\/2020\/10\/25.-Fluorosis-of-the-Cervical-Spine-_151-157.pdf\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/nimhans.ac.in\/wp-content\/uploads\/2020\/10\/25.-Fluorosis-of-the-Cervical-Spine-_151-157.pdf\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #212121; font-family: inherit;\"\u003ECERVIVAL SPONDYLOSIS CAUSING VERTEBROBASILAR INSUFFICIENCY-\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cdiv style=\"text-align: left;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit;\"\u003E\"Although the most common aetiology of transient vertebrobasilar insufficiency is atherosclerosis, a similar syndrome may occasionally be produced by cervical osteophytes. The possibility of such a remedial lesion makes further investigation mandatory in such patients—especially if symptoms are associated with sudden movements of the head or neck\"\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #212121; font-family: inherit;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC493808\/\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC493808\/\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"color: #212121; font-family: inherit;\"\u003EFLUOROSIS MIMICKING CERVICAL SPONDYLOSIS-\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/span\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"font-family: inherit;\"\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; color: #212121;\"\u003ESkeletal fluorosis can mimic various arthritis such as rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis or spondyloarthropathy.\u003C\/span\u003E\u003Cspan style=\"background-color: white; box-sizing: inherit; color: #212121; line-height: 0; position: relative; top: -0.5em; vertical-align: baseline;\"\u003E\u003Ca aria-expanded=\"false\" aria-haspopup=\"true\" class=\"bibr popnode\" href=\"https:\/\/www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov\/pmc\/articles\/PMC9450208\/#B3\" rid=\"B3\" role=\"button\" style=\"background-color: transparent; font-size: 15px;\"\u003EThis is an online E log book to discuss our patient's de-identified health data shared after taking his\/her\/guardian's signed informed consent. Here we discuss our individual patient's problems through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patient's clinical problems with collective current best evidence based inputs. This E log book also reflects my patient-centered online learning portfolio.\u003C\/span\u003E\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOSCE\/discussion-\u0026nbsp;\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/shaardul124.blogspot.com\/2023\/12\/osce.html\"\u003Ehttps:\/\/shaardul124.blogspot.com\/2023\/12\/osce.html\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E63 year old housewife from Nalgonda\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EChief complaints- Vomiting 5 episodes 3 days ago\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EHistory of present illness-\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient was apparently alright 1 year back then developed vomiting associated with giddiness and pain. she came to our hospital and vomiting subsided with treatment. She was asked to take Vertin 24 (betahistine) at discharge. she took the medication for 3 months and then stopped after consulting with her physician. She had mild episodes of vomiting for the next months until 3 days back when she had 5 episodes (severe)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EVomiting- non projectile, contents were food\/watery. there was no blood present in the vomitus. no temporal association with meal timings was noticed. it was associated with giddiness and colicky, non radiating pain in the epigastrium, present only during the episode. Not associated with fever, headache, diarrhoea or constipation.\u0026nbsp;\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFrequency of stools are normal but volume is decreased due to less food intake out of fear of vomiting.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo history of- abdominal distention, heart burn, acidity, excessive flatulence, jaundice.\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGiddiness- there was no history of headache, trauma, fall, stroke, aural fullness, tinnitus, no positional variation or triggering factors (starts randomly). no aggravating factors. relieved with medications.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPast history-\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient is a known case of hypertension since 5 years, is on medication Telma 40.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo history of tuberculosis, diabetes mellitus, stroke.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPersonal history-\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EMixed diet\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EReduced appetite\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EAdequate sleep\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBowel movements are of normal frequency but reduced volume\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBladder movements are normal\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ENo addictions or allergies\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EOccasionally drinks toddy.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDaily routine (premorbid)\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E0500- wakes up\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E0500-0600- gets ready\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E0730- Chai + bun\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E0730- 1300- stays indoors, doesn't do much\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1100- Rice+ curry\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1300- Buttermilk+rice\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E1300-2000- stays indoors, doesn't do much\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003E2000- Rice+curry\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Emorbid changes- doesn't eat much due to fear of vomiting, however, small meals are consumed regularly.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFamily history- No similar complaints in the family. no history of HTN or DM in the family.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EGeneral examination-\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPatient is concious coheret cooperative and oriented to time place and person.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Ebuilt- average\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003Enourishment- average\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPallor is present, icterus, cyanosis, clubbing, lymphadenopathy or edema are absent.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ETemperature- Afebrile\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EPR- 78 bpm, regular, normal volume, normal character, no radioradial delay, no radiofemoral delay.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003ERR- 17 cpm\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EBP- 130\/80 mmHg\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EDecreased range of motion of neck flexion\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/p\u003E\u003Cp\u003EFixed flexion deformity of
